claims.dashboard_text: The United States produced and consumed more than 57 million metric tons of plastic in 2019, while less than 7% was recovered for reuse.
claims.misuse_guardrail: This is a modeled 2019 economy-wide material-flow result, not a 2026 annual statistic or EPA MSW total.

claims.dashboard_text: The leading individually reported U.S. resin consumption estimates for 2019 were PP 8.6, HDPE 7.9, LLDPE 5.7, and PVC 5.2 million metric tons.
claims.misuse_guardrail: Do not infer current rank or sum these values as total plastic consumption.

claims.dashboard_text: Packaging was the largest named 2019 U.S. application at 17.2 MMT; building and construction used 8.3 MMT.
claims.misuse_guardrail: Use categories are modeled flows into use and do not equal same-year waste.

claims.dashboard_text: EPA's 2018 municipal-solid-waste series reports 35.68 million U.S. tons of plastic generated, 3.09 recycled, 5.62 combusted for energy, and 26.97 landfilled.
claims.misuse_guardrail: Units are U.S. short tons and scope is MSW; do not combine with the 2019 economy-wide MFA.

claims.dashboard_text: The National Academies estimated 1.13-2.24 MMT of U.S. plastic waste entered the environment in 2016 and documented ingestion or entanglement among 914 species.
claims.misuse_guardrail: The range is an estimate with uncertainty; the species count is documentation of exposure/effect pathways, not an extinction count.

claims.dashboard_text: Commodity plastics are produced through distinct precursor chains: ethylene to PE, propylene to PP, ethylene glycol plus terephthalic acid to PET, and chlorine/ethylene through EDC and VCM to PVC.
claims.misuse_guardrail: These are pathway summaries; plant technology, regional feedstock, coproduct allocation, and additives vary.

claims.dashboard_text: Approximate cross-database cradle-to-resin water-consumption ranges are 3.3-44.4 L/kg for PET, 5.9-24.1 for HDPE, and 5.2-20.5 for PP.
claims.misuse_guardrail: Values were read approximately from a figure; they are database results, not universal plant coefficients.

claims.dashboard_text: Life-cycle databases can produce materially different water results for the same resin because geography, allocation, technology, cooling-water recycling, and system boundaries differ.
claims.misuse_guardrail: Do not average incompatible values without a harmonization protocol.

claims.dashboard_text: Avoiding one million kilograms of virgin resin corresponds to gross cradle-to-resin water ranges of about 3.3-44.4 million L PET, 5.9-24.1 million L HDPE, or 5.2-20.5 million L PP.
claims.misuse_guardrail: This multiplication excludes replacement production, washing, logistics, product loss, and end of life, so it is not net water savings.

claims.dashboard_text: A national net water-saving estimate for plastic replacement remains unavailable because dominant replacement systems lack harmonized functional-unit and geographic inventories.
claims.misuse_guardrail: Do not turn this evidence gap into a zero-impact assumption.

claims.dashboard_text: Plastic particles have been reported in foods and human samples, but current evidence does not yet establish quantitative health risk at measured food levels.
claims.misuse_guardrail: Neither declare safety nor claim all real-world exposure is proven harmful; show the method and dose-response gaps.

claims.dashboard_text: In one carotid-surgery cohort, detected plaque micro/nanoplastics were associated with a higher composite risk of heart attack, stroke, or death (adjusted HR 4.53; 95% CI 2.00-10.27).
claims.misuse_guardrail: This selected observational cohort cannot prove causation, ingestion route, source, or general-population risk.

claims.dashboard_text: A Faroese cohort linked higher prenatal and childhood PFAS serum concentrations to lower tetanus and diphtheria antibody responses; it did not measure maternal microplastic ingestion or show universal vaccine failure.
claims.misuse_guardrail: PFAS chemicals are not synonymous with microplastic particles or all plastics; findings are observational and outcome-specific.

claims.dashboard_text: High-confidence chemical hazards exist in plastic supply chains, including carcinogenic classifications for vinyl chloride and concerns for styrene and acrylonitrile, plus occupational isocyanate sensitization and asthma.
claims.misuse_guardrail: A monomer or reactive-precursor hazard does not establish the same exposure or risk from every cured finished article.

claims.dashboard_text: EPA found that certain fluorination processes used on HDPE containers can form and leach PFAS; this finding does not apply to every HDPE product.
claims.misuse_guardrail: Always retain the qualifiers certain, fluorinated, and process-specific.

claims.dashboard_text: The EU, France, Germany, and Rwanda use combinations of targeted restrictions, reuse, deposits, producer responsibility, collection, and exceptions rather than eliminating every plastic use.
claims.misuse_guardrail: Do not describe any listed jurisdiction as plastic-free or treat legal targets as achieved water savings.

claims.dashboard_text: DOE modeled 0.38 billion dry metric tons per year of U.S. macroalgae supply at or below $1,000 per dry ton under a 50% productive-area assumption.
claims.misuse_guardrail: This is modeled potential, not production, a forecast, sustainable harvest, or finished bioplastic output.

claims.dashboard_text: U.S. seaweed aquaculture remains developmental; NOAA reports an Alaska example exceeding 112,000 lb in 2019, in wet rather than dry weight.
claims.misuse_guardrail: Do not compare this wet harvest directly with DOE dry-biomass potential.

claims.dashboard_text: Seaweed cultivation may avoid irrigation, but one 2026 film LCA found substantial conversion wastewater and higher water use than its LDPE comparator.
claims.misuse_guardrail: One formulation does not represent all seaweed materials; never call seaweed plastic water-free.

claims.dashboard_text: A defensible transition starts with unnecessary products, scales reuse and high capture, controls hazardous chemistry, and evaluates substitution on a product-service functional unit.
claims.misuse_guardrail: This is a decision framework, not evidence that every reuse or substitute system is lower-impact.

claims.dashboard_text: Material substitution can shift burdens: a 2024 study found plastics had lower greenhouse-gas impacts in 15 of 16 modeled applications, while not resolving water, toxicity, litter, or biodiversity tradeoffs.
claims.misuse_guardrail: Do not use a greenhouse-gas comparison to dismiss other impacts or endorse all plastic uses.
